name: ESW World Championship
epitaph: The fed's top belt. Eddie won it as the NYCW World title at the first Kick Ass Inc on 3 March 2003, and it runs through the change of name to the ESW and forty-one reigns in the fed's table to Craig Williams on 15 September 2010, among them Slipstream's five and Darien Sunn's record 230 days. The table's footnote says it was merged with the CWA and BLPW World titles to become the Triple Crown Championship.
notes: The page's footnote: 'The ESW World title was merged with the CWA World title and the BLPW World title to become the Triple Crown Championship.'

name: ESW Television Championship
epitaph: Devo won the first Television title in a fifteen-man over-the-top battle royal at the second Kick Ass Inc on 7 April 2003. Its table runs through forty-two reigns to Vise on 28 September 2010, and the holders include Rayne, the first to hold both the World and Television titles, Exodus, whose 189 days stood as the record, and Kid Krazy, who held it four times.

name: ESW Survivor Championship
epitaph: Steve Sinclair created the Survivor title on 10 November 2003, when the NYCW Tag Team titles were dropped, and appointed Kid Krazy its first champion; the fed's rules call it 'a gimmick themed title'. Its table runs through forty-six reigns to Amber LeBeau on 15 September 2010, among them Tommy Purr's 242 days in 2009, the longest run of any belt in the fed, and Steve Sinclair's own reign in September 2008.

name: ESW Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Eddie and Kid Krazy won the first Tag Team titles at Kick Ass Inc on 30 June 2003, and Steve Sinclair put the belts on the shelf on 10 November 2003 when the two stopped being partners. They came back as a yearly one-night tournament held at the Bruise Cruise, the way the fed's own history says the King of the Ring is run, and its table lists eight champions from 2003 to the Gary Barber and Shawn Sanders pairing of 2010.

name: ESW Queen of the Ring Championship
epitaph: The fed's women's title opens in its table on 13 September 2009, when RC Pride beat Orloc at Pyrophoric, and runs through five reigns in a year: Bombshell, Kira Yakamoto and Bishop Spade between RC Pride's two reigns, the last won at Lethal Lottery on 15 September 2010.
